reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents ABP Uncut-style entertainment-news or current-affairs reporting about Sushant Singh Rajput's relationships and related case updates. The presenter format and celebrity-photo montage support that context, while the channel-subscription request and invitation to comment are ordinary engagement prompts rather than conditions for a financial or data-related offer.

citations.quote: What is the role of Ankita Lokhande in Sushant Singh Rajput Case? , Rhea Chakraborty | ABP Uncut
Today in this video we will see how the relationship was in Sushant's life.
We will keep updating all the updates on this whole case

opening.argument: The description directly pairs a viewer action with the channel’s distribution pathway: “Subscribe our channel” appears alongside a subscription URL. That is a low-barrier acquisition flow presented to viewers, and the video also promises that viewers can watch to learn how the relationships and case developed. Although no cash reward is stated, the combination of a requested action, an external subscription link, and a promised informational payoff leaves open whether the content is primarily designed to drive participation rather than provide neutral reporting. The judge should therefore treat this as a possible low-barrier acquisition solicitation, even if the evidence does not establish a financial loss.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference argument calls the subscription request ordinary engagement, but it does not explain why the request is placed directly beside an external subscription URL and a promise to reveal compelling case details. Its entertainment-news framing describes the subject, not the function of the call to action. The absence of a stated cash payment does not by itself rule out a low-barrier acquisition scheme; it only makes this category a limited fit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The subscription request is plainly a request to follow a news channel, not a promise of money, an asset, or a reward. The description identifies the channel as a news outlet, and the cited URL is a YouTube channel-subscription link. Nothing connects subscribing to a withdrawal, payment, verification, or other benefit. The opening therefore fails to establish the required reward-action relationship.

Subscribe our channel: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMPHDQznmQL72WJ2WJ2UYINW5W?Sub_confirmation=1

opening.argument: Several engagement signals appear together: an external subscription URL, a direct request to subscribe, and repeated promises of continuing updates about a highly charged case. The description also directs viewers to multiple external properties, including a live site and app links. None of this proves fraud, but the accumulation of external pathways and urgency-adjacent breaking-news framing creates a plausible risk that viewers are being moved from attention to participation. Under a cautious reading, the content does not clearly rule out a low-barrier acquisition funnel, even though no financial return is shown.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense relies on the absence of an explicit financial offer, but the relevant concern is the combined presentation: sensational case coverage, repeated updates, and several off-video destinations. Calling these links ordinary does not address why viewers are directed to a subscription page, live site, and app download in the same package. At minimum, the evidence leaves a participation funnel insufficiently excluded.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited links are transparent official-channel destinations: a YouTube subscription, the channel’s live site, and an app-store listing. The description says the outlet provides news and coverage, while the narration says it will keep updating the case. Those are ordinary distribution mechanisms, not evidence of a reward, payment, investment, or deceptive acquisition flow. The argument converts normal media promotion into a scam signal without a concrete prohibited promise.

opening.argument: The material can be read as promotional packaging built around celebrity-case attention rather than merely discussion. The title poses a provocative question about a named person’s role, the description says viewers should watch to know how the relationships developed, and the narration promises ongoing updates while asking what viewers think. That structure steers viewers toward continued engagement and channel subscription. The entertainment-news label does not itself exclude a promotional acquisition purpose; it may be the vehicle used to make the solicitation feel credible and low risk.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the presenter format and celebrity photographs as proof of ordinary reporting, but those same devices can package a solicitation as trusted news. The title’s question, the promise to reveal relationship details, and the invitation to comment all keep the viewer in an engagement loop. The reference side does not establish that the promotional function is incidental; it assumes it from the genre label.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The content’s role is supported by its explicit subject matter: relationships, an FIR, and continuing case updates. A provocative title and a request for comments are normal editorial engagement devices, and the channel description identifies a broad news operation with coverage across current affairs and entertainment. No purchase, deposit, reward, or claim of income is presented. Reframing ordinary audience engagement as a scam does not supply the missing scam mechanism.
